hypothesis: In plaice, mean Fulton condition factor k = W/L^3 binned by length rises to an interior maximum near 30 cm and then declines at larger sizes, rather than being constant.
pass_criterion: Using DATRAS individual plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) records with length and weight, compute mean k = 100*W(g)/L(cm)^3 per 1-cm class (n>=30 per class, 10-60 cm), pooled across surveys and sexes. Pass if all hold: (a) the LOESS-smoothed peak of k lies at 25-35 cm; (b) peak k exceeds mean k in the 12-15 cm classes by at least 5%; (c) mean k in 45-55 cm is at least 3% below peak k; (d) the bootstrap 95% CI of the peak length lies strictly inside 20-40 cm.
fail_criterion: Fail if k is monotonic across length classes, or the smoothed peak length falls outside 25-35 cm, or peak k is less than 5% above k at 12-15 cm, or k at 45-55 cm is within 3% of the peak or higher.
interpretation: Thompson's k is the Fulton condition factor (W/L^3, scaled by 100). Size of fish is total length in cm. The 'size at which maturity begins' (about 30 cm) is tested only as the location of the k maximum within 25-35 cm; the maturity stage field may be used as a descriptive cross-check but is not a pass condition. Modern reinterpretation: Thompson's data were early 20th-century North Sea samples; DATRAS survey samples are seasonal (mainly quarters 1 and 3), so seasonal condition variation may shift k, and analysis should be stratified by quarter as a sensitivity check.

dataset.name: DATRAS - Database of Trawl Surveys
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS provides downloadable exchange data and web services for North Sea trawl surveys (e.g. NS-IBTS, BTS). Biological (CA) records include species, length class, individual weight, sex and maturity, so k per length class for Pleuronectes platessa can be computed.
